title: There was a time when you were not even mentioned.
subtitle: Before you existed
then: The Prophet ﷺ used to recite this surah in the Friday dawn prayer, as Ibn Abbas reported in Sahih Muslim. Ibn Kathir says Allah brought man into being {trap}after he was not even a thing worth mentioning, because of his lowliness and weakness.{/trap} {idea}The surah opens with a question you can only answer yes.{/idea}
now: Your name is on your ID, your email, your work badge. People tag you in photos. It feels like you have always been someone. {idea}A short while ago, no one on earth could have said your name.{/idea}
old: I have always been here, and I am owed my place.
new: I was nothing worth mentioning, then Allah mentioned me into being.
try: Say Alhamdulillah for simply existing, once, slowly, before you sleep.

title: Made from a mixed drop, given ears and eyes, to be tested.
subtitle: Why you were given hearing and sight
then: Ibn Abbas said the mixed drop is {idea}the fluid of the man and the woman when they meet and mix{/idea}, then man changes stage to stage. Ibn Kathir says hearing and sight were given {trap}so he could use them for obedience or disobedience.{/trap}
now: Your earbuds are in all day. Your eyes are on a screen for hours. Those are the two gifts this verse names. {idea}Every song, every clip, every page is part of an exam you did not notice you were sitting.{/idea}
old: My eyes and ears are mine to use however I want.
new: My eyes and ears were given for a test. What I feed them is my answer.
try: Choose one thing to listen to or watch today that you would want counted for you.

title: The way was shown. Grateful or ungrateful is your part.
subtitle: Guidance given, choice left open
then: Ibn Kathir says "We guided him" means {idea}We explained it, made it clear, and showed it to him{/idea}: the path of good and the path of evil. He cites the hadith: {trap}every person wakes up as a merchant of his own soul, either ruining it or setting it free.{/trap}
now: Your alarm rings. Before you open your eyes, the day is already a market. How you speak to your kids, what you do with your lunch hour, what you say about a coworker. {idea}Each one is a small trade with your own soul.{/idea}
old: I never really got a clear picture of what is right.
new: The way has been shown. Today I choose gratitude or not.
try: When you wake tomorrow, say one line of thanks before you touch your phone.

title: For the ungrateful path, chains and a blaze.
subtitle: One end of the fork, named briefly
then: Having said man is either grateful or ungrateful, the surah names the end of the second path in one verse. Ibn Kathir says {trap}Sa'ir is the flame and fire of Hell.{/trap} Then, at once, {idea}the surah spends many verses on the righteous.{/idea}
now: You tell yourself no one can chain you: you do what you want, when you want. But the late-night habit, the temper, the debt you keep feeding already feel heavy. {idea}Ingratitude starts as freedom and ends as chains.{/idea}
old: Living without limits is real freedom.
new: Turning from Allah ends in chains. Gratitude is the real freedom.
try: Name one habit that already feels like a chain, and loosen it one notch today.

title: The righteous drink a cup mixed with camphor.
subtitle: Cool, fragrant, delicious

key.label: The other end of the fork

then: Right after the blaze comes a cool drink. Ibn Kathir says camphor is known for being {reward}cooling and fragrant, and in Paradise its taste will be delicious.{/reward} The contrast is deliberate: {idea}fire for one path, coolness for the other.{/idea}
now: A long fasting day in summer. The first sip of cold water at sunset. Nothing in the world tastes better. {reward}That is a hint of what this verse promises.{/reward}
old: Doing right is all effort and no taste.
new: The righteous path ends in a sweetness I can barely imagine.
try: With your next cold drink, say Bismillah and remember this cup.

title: A spring they direct wherever they wish.
subtitle: Abundance under their control
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah's close servants {reward}drink from it directly, to their fill.{/reward} Mujahid said {idea}they will divert it wherever they wish{/idea}: to their castles, homes, and sitting rooms.
now: The water bill. The tap that runs slow in summer. The bottle you carry because you are never sure. {reward}This verse describes water that never runs out and goes where you send it.{/reward}
old: Good things are always scarce and I have to fight for them.
new: For Allah's servants, there is a spring that never runs short.
try: Give someone water today, a glass, a bottle, a donation to a well.

title: They keep their promises and fear a spreading Day.
subtitle: The first trait of the righteous
then: Ibn Kathir says they worship Allah with what is required and {idea}also by fulfilling what they vowed.{/idea} Qatadah said the evil of that Day {trap}will spread until it fills the heavens and the earth.{/trap} Their fear of it shapes what they do now.
now: You said "if this works out, I will give to charity." It worked out. Weeks passed. {idea}The righteous are the ones who remember what they promised Allah when things got better.{/idea}
old: A promise to Allah made in a hard moment can be forgotten later.
new: Keeping my word to Allah, even a small one, marks the righteous.
try: Remember one promise you made to Allah and do part of it today.

title: They give away food they themselves want.
subtitle: Feeding the poor, the orphan, the captive
then: Mujahid said they give food {idea}while they themselves love it and desire it.{/idea} Ibn Kathir cites the hadith: {reward}the best charity is given while you are healthy and stingy, hoping to be rich and fearing poverty.{/reward} The captive, some said, included non-Muslim prisoners.
now: You bought the good dates for yourself. Someone at the door, or a neighbor having a hard month, comes to mind. Giving the cheap box is easy. {reward}Giving the one you were looking forward to is the verse.{/reward}
old: I give once I have more than enough.
new: The giving that counts most is the giving that costs me something I want.
try: Give away one thing today that you actually like, food, a meal, your time.

title: We want no payback, not even a thank you.
subtitle: Giving for Allah's Face alone
then: Ibn Kathir says they seek no reward and {trap}do not want to be thanked in front of people.{/trap} Mujahid and Sa'id bin Jubayr said: {idea}they did not say this with their tongues. Allah knew it in their hearts and praised them for it.{/idea}
now: You helped your friend move all Saturday. They did not say thanks. It stings for days. {idea}This verse asks: who did you do it for?{/idea}
old: If no one thanks me, my good deed was wasted.
new: When I give for Allah, a missing thank you takes nothing away.
try: Do one kind thing today and tell no one about it.

title: Their giving is shaped by fear of a frowning Day.
subtitle: The hard, long Day they prepare for
then: Ibn Kathir says they do it {idea}so that perhaps Allah will have mercy on them on that Day.{/idea} Ibn Abbas said 'abus means {trap}difficult{/trap} and qamtarir means {trap}long.{/trap} Others said faces will frown and foreheads tighten from dismay.
now: You worry at night about death, about the Day, about whether you are good enough. The worry just sits there. {idea}These people turned the same worry into a plate of food for someone hungry.{/idea}
old: Fearing the Day just makes me anxious.
new: Fear of the Day can become a reason to be kind today.
try: Next time you feel that fear, turn it into one act of giving.

title: Saved from the Day they feared, given light and joy.
subtitle: Radiant faces, happy hearts
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah {reward}protected them from what they feared{/reward} and gave them {reward}radiance in their faces and joy in their hearts.{/reward} He notes that a happy heart lights the face, as Ka'b bin Malik described the Prophet's ﷺ face shining like a piece of the moon when he was happy.
now: You have seen it: the face of someone who just gave something big away. A mother after feeding a crowd. {idea}Joy inside shows on the outside.{/idea} The Day will show it fully.
old: Giving things away leaves me with less.
new: What I give for Allah comes back as light in my face and joy in my heart.
try: Notice how you feel after the next thing you give. Thank Allah for it.

title: Their reward is because they were patient.
subtitle: Patience in leaving their desires
then: Ibn Kathir says because of their patience Allah gives them {reward}a spacious home, a delightful life, and fine clothing.{/reward} When this verse was recited to Abu Sulayman Ad-Darani, he said: {idea}because they were patient in leaving off their desires in the world.{/idea}
now: You wanted the expensive thing and bought the plain one so you could give. You wanted to sleep and stood up to pray. {idea}Nobody saw it as patience. Allah did.{/idea}
old: Saying no to what I want is just loss.
new: Every desire I leave for Allah is patience, and patience is paid.
try: Say no to one small desire today, and give it to Allah.
